title: Target lock
subtitle: Build a readable target lock with a reachable response and a useful recovery.
summary: The boss selects a player or position.
overview: The boss selects a player or position, communicates that selection, and commits a later attack to it, creating a window for deliberate placement.
learning: Tune the signal, commitment, geometry, response, and recovery of a target lock as one rule.

demo.title: Test the target lock
phaseDescriptions: Use a persistent marker and a clear lock moment that distinguishes tracking before commitment from the fixed target after commitment.
The marked player moves the attack away, shares or transfers responsibility if supported, or waits for commitment before leaving the area.
The marker is consumed at the committed location and cannot follow the player after lock; a short reset separates that resolution from the next selection.

steps.title: Can the player read the complete rule?
steps.body: Use a persistent marker and a clear lock moment that distinguishes tracking before commitment from the fixed target after commitment.

steps.title: Is the intended response reachable?
steps.body: The marked player moves the attack away, shares or transfers responsibility if supported, or waits for commitment before leaving the area.

steps.title: Does recovery create a useful outcome?
steps.body: The marker is consumed at the committed location and cannot follow the player after lock; a short reset separates that resolution from the next selection.

mistakes.title: Continuing to retarget after the lock cue teaches players that the marker has no dependable meaning
mistakes.body: Continuing to retarget after the lock cue teaches players that the marker has no dependable meaning.

mistakes.title: The cue and active geometry disagree
mistakes.body: If the visible target lock cue promises a different area or timing, the player cannot carry the learned rule into the next cycle.

designNotes.title: Tune the complete rule
designNotes.body: Tune selection range, tracking duration, lock delay, attack delay, and multiplayer priority rules so responsibility remains legible.

designNotes.title: Escalate one variable at a time
designNotes.body: Lock several targets, attach different outcomes to markers, or shorten the placement window while keeping commitment explicit.

designNotes.title: Prove the recovery
designNotes.body: The marker is consumed at the committed location and cannot follow the player after lock; a short reset separates that resolution from the next selection.

story.title: What the mechanic communicates
story.body: The boss selects a player or position, communicates that selection, and commits a later attack to it, creating a window for deliberate placement. The encounter uses that rule as a short promise: a visible signal, a committed action, and a result the player can verify.

adaptation.title: Adapt it to the player verbs
adaptation.body: The marked player moves the attack away, shares or transfers responsibility if supported, or waits for commitment before leaving the area. Tune selection range, tracking duration, lock delay, attack delay, and multiplayer priority rules so responsibility remains legible.

distinction.title: Keep the mechanic distinct
distinction.body: Continuing to retarget after the lock cue teaches players that the marker has no dependable meaning. Do not hide that distinction behind extra effects or tracking that the announced rule does not contain.

lensNotes.body: The signal must reveal the relevant timing and geometry before commitment.
After commitment, the rule stops changing in ways the signal did not announce.
Preparation, action, and recovery create a legible cycle of pressure and release.
The response uses an ordinary supported verb and produces an observable result.
